newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN SHOE SELLER BRANTANO EYES EURO EXPANSION.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN SHOE SELLER BRANTANO EYES EURO EXPANSION.

text.p: Belgian shoe distributor Brantano said on Wednesday the listing of 40 percent of its stock at next month's planned initial public offering on the Brussels bourse would groom it for expansion in Europe.
"A capital increase is out of the question. It's just...placing 40 percent of the shares," chief executive officer Joris Brantegem told a news conference.
He said a prospectus and details of the listing would be presented at a road show on May 28.
Bookbuilding for institutional investors starts on May 29. The book building period will be followed by a public offering.
"The reason for this event is of course growth...in Europe," said Brantegem.
"But we will not pin ourselves down to France, we'll also look at growth markets in Europe," he said.
He said Brantano had already carried out market research.
"We know all the players in Europe," he said.
Brantano, which has a workforce of 640 -- representing 558 full-time equivalents -- will enter foreign markets cautiously, Brantegem said.
"Every market has its own habits, collections," he said.
Chairman Kurt Moons said the group, with 102 selling points in Belgium and three test shops in France, generated enough cash flow "to carry out certain (takeover) transactions".
Brantano, which sold 3.3 million pairs of shoes in 1996, had a 1996 net current profit of 173 million francs ($4.9 million) and 324 million francs ($9.2 million) net cash flow.

Turnover rose to 3.375 billion francs ($95.8 million) in 1996 from 2.675 billion ($75.9 million) a year earlier. Own funds are 645 million francs ($(18.3 million) and capital excluding reserves 150 million ($4.3 million).
Its market share rose 70 percent over the past three years to about nine percent.
Brantegem said the total Belgian shoe distribution market was worth 38.6 billion francs ($1.1 billion) but had narrowed from 42 billion francs ($1.19 billion) two years ago.
Retail shoe shops account for 52 percent of total sales, the larger chains for the rest, he said.
